parts.t: Neighbourhood guide · City of Surrey · Newton

Sullivan Station is an MLS® area in the southeast part of Newton. It covers roughly 144 to 152 Street between about 56 and 64 Avenue, and along 152 Street it reaches south to at least 52 to 55 Avenue. East Newton is to the north, across 64 Avenue. It sits within the City’s former South Newton plan area.

Written by Jared Gibbons, REALTOR®, Royal LePage Little Oak Realty, on October 13, 2026. I have worked in Fraser Valley real estate for 11+ years. Rules and boundaries change, so confirm anything important with the City of Surrey and Surrey Schools.
Not legal, planning or financial advice. Confirm zoning, plan designations and school catchments before you buy or sell.

blocks.text: Homes for sale in Sullivan Station

parts.t: Sullivan Station is a family-oriented part of Surrey. The housing runs from modern detached homes to townhouses and newer developments, and the strong schools, parks and residential feel draw buyers who want space, value and long-term growth in Sullivan Station.

Townhomes, family properties and newer construction homes all show up in the current Sullivan Station MLS listings on this page. The page refreshes regularly, so the prices, photos and full property details stay current.

blocks.text: What to look at in a Sullivan Station home

parts.t: These are the questions I go through with buyers.
Lot size, the age of the roof, furnace, plumbing and wiring, and drainage
What the zone allows, and whether any suite was built with a permit
Assuming you can add a suite or rebuild just because a neighbour did
Strata fees, the depreciation report (the plan for future repairs), meeting minutes and bylaws
About upcoming special levies (extra one-time charges) and what the fees include

items.t: Pet, rental or age rules that don’t fit your plans

parts.t: Zoning and plan designations can be different for each lot.

This comes from MLS® sales data, not an official source. The median lot size for detached houses that sold between July 1 and October 8, 2026 came to 3,713 square feet, drawn from 26 sales that included a recorded lot size.
The South Newton plan was approved in 1999. The City says it has been rescinded and the Official Community Plan now guides building here.
The City says the area has several fish-bearing creeks, including the headwaters of Archibald Creek and Sullivan Heights Creek.
